verdict.rationale: LightSprint's core interaction is natural language. Users describe a change in plain English and the product builds it, spins up a live preview, and prepares it for review. Users can also plan larger features before handing them off as tasks, send background cloud agents at bug backlogs, and create tasks from Slack, Linear or Jira. Missing for 10: evidence that product operations beyond code changes (settings, rollback, board management) can be driven by natural language, since rollback is described as a UI control; no independent or hands-on corroboration of how well plain-English commands work.
